title: async iteration and for-await-of
learningObjectives: Explain async iteration and for-await-of and implement reliable browser event and network workflows.

understand.concept: An async iterable exposes Symbol.asyncIterator, returning an async iterator whose next() result is a Promise. for await...of consumes asynchronous values sequentially. It can also consume synchronous iterables.
understand.whyItMatters: Async iteration is useful for streams and delayed sequences. Sequential consumption can pace work but may be slower than parallel processing when tasks are independent.
understand.analogy: An async iterator prepares each next item when the consumer asks for it.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; JavaScript scheduling, HTTP semantics, and browser security follow platform standards.

explain.narrative: The loop awaits each next result before continuing.

examples.code: async function* updates(){yield 'connected';await new Promise(r=>setTimeout(r,50));yield 'ready'}async function show(){for await(const item of updates())console.log(item)}show();
examples.explanation: The loop awaits each next result before continuing.
examples.expectedOutput: Console or UI output demonstrates the concept; network examples require a configured endpoint.

practise.guidedTask: Create an async generator with delayed updates and consume it with for await...of. Add error handling.
practise.independentTask: Build an asynchronous feature with explicit states, cancellation, and error handling. Document which failures are safe to retry.
hints: Separate HTTP errors from network and parsing errors.
Use bounded retries only for suitable operations.
Tie UI updates to the latest active request.
